speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your tummy looks swollen. Can you tell me if you are vomiting anything yellow or green, or if you have been passing gas and having bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds very painful for him. Has he been passing any gas or having bowel movements, and if so, what do they look like? Also, have you noticed anything unusual with his stools, such as them being very foul-smelling or floating?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful to know; the absence of fever and diarrhea makes an acute infection less likely. Has the baby passed any stool recently, and if so, was it foul-smelling or did you notice any blood or mucus? Also, please describe the exact sound of his crying when his abdomen is touched.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of normal stool passage and worsening abdominal distension are concerning signs. Has the baby ever passed "currant jelly" stools (dark red blood and mucus), and is there a history of intermittent, severe episodes of crying where he draws his legs up?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray results showing dilated bowel segments with an absent rectal gas pattern strongly suggest a mechanical obstruction. Given the baby's age, lack of meconium passage, and signs of severe pain, this is highly concerning for Hirschsprung's disease. Have you noticed any family history of this condition, and did he ever pass his first stool within the first 48 hours after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's Disease (likely with distal enterocolis given the acute distension and pain).

The X-ray findings of dilated loops and absent rectal gas, combined with the history of delayed meconium passage and severe pain on palpation, strongly support this diagnosis.
